name: Extract intents from prose
description: propose(prose, { submittedBy }) creates the next proposal file in .lastro/proposals/ with status open and sends the prose and the current use cases to an LLM through an AskJson transport with a fixed system prompt and JSON Schema (step "extract"). The answer lists intents, each the addition, removal or change of exactly one use case: id (P-n.I-nn), slug, name, a natural-language description of the change, change (add, modify or remove), the use case (an existing id, or a newly reserved id and slug for an add), a provability (formal, empirical, beyond-proof), a beyondProofReason ("none" or one of the five reasons) and a verbatim quote, and replaces: the existing proofs of that use case the new behavior contradicts, each with a reason (extraction receives every touched use case with its proofs in readable notation; for a remove the SDK lists every proof of the use case itself); one resulting use case per touched use case with its name and, for add and modify, the complete new description (after), all its intents combined, and the intents that produce it; decisions that reference intents by zero-based index; and notPromised items. The SDK fills each modify and remove with the use case's current description (before); the LLM never supplies it. The proposal (lastro: proposal/v1) records the baseline (sha256 over the canonical use cases without their proofs), the submitter, every intent proposed with no approvals, decisions D1, D2... with origin extraction, and the review policy. Intents have no kind. Without an LLM transport or a custom extractor, propose() throws.
